    First CourseSecond CourseThird CourseFourth Course
    First CourseNever-hungry-again radishes on buttermilk biscuitsScarlett swears she'll never go hungry. Crisp radishes on salted butter and biscuits.How to make it250g self-raising flour80g cold butter, cubed, plus 100g softened for spreading200ml buttermilk2 bunches of radishes, trimmed1 tsp sea salt flakes2 tbsp chives, snippedRub the cold butter into the flour with a pinch of salt, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough.Pat out 3cm thick, cut rounds and bake at 220°C until risen and golden.Slice the radishes thinly.Split the warm biscuits, spread thickly with soft butter and pile on radishes, salt flakes and chives.Gold-bid devilled eggsRhett bids $150 in gold for one dance. Golden yolks whipped with mustard and paprika.How to make it8 eggs4 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise2 tsp Dijon mustard1 tsp white wine vinegar1 tsp smoked paprika1 tbsp chives, snippedLower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, then cool in iced water.Peel, halve and mash the yolks with the mayo, mustard, vinegar and salt.Pipe or spoon back into the whites.Dust with paprika and scatter with chives.Hot corn muffins with honey butterTomorrow is another day.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Second CourseTwelve Oaks barbecue pork shoulderThe Wilkes barbecue at Twelve Oaks. Slow-roast pork shoulder with vinegar slaw.How to make it2kg boneless pork shoulder2 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp smoked paprika1 tsp garlic powder150ml cider vinegar1 tsp chilli flakes1/2 white cabbage, finely shredded2 carrots, grated8 soft white rollsRub the pork with the sugar, paprika, garlic powder and plenty of salt.Roast covered at 160°C until it pulls apart easily.Warm 100ml of the vinegar with the chilli flakes and a pinch of sugar for a sauce.Toss the cabbage and carrot with the rest of the vinegar and salt.Pull the pork, splash with the chilli vinegar and serve with the slaw and rolls.Green velvet drapes herb-crusted lambScarlett's dress from the green drapes. Lamb racks under a bright green herb crust.How to make it2 lamb racks, 8 cutlets each1 cup flat-leaf parsley1/2 cup mint leaves2 garlic cloves60g fresh breadcrumbs3 tbsp olive oil2 tbsp Dijon mustard500g baby potatoes30g butterBlitz the parsley, mint, garlic, breadcrumbs and 2 tbsp oil to a bright green crumb.Sear the lamb racks all over in the rest of the oil, then brush with mustard and press on the crumb.Roast at 200°C until pink in the middle, then rest.Boil the potatoes, toss with butter and serve with the carved cutlets.Third CourseFiddle-dee-dee Georgia peach cobblerFiddle-dee-dee to all the war talk. Baked peaches under a buttermilk crust with cream.How to make it6 ripe yellow peaches, sliced80g brown sugar1 tbsp cornflour1 tsp ground cinnamon200g self-raising flour80g cold butter, cubed50g caster sugar150ml buttermilk300ml pouring creamToss the peaches with the brown sugar, cornflour and cinnamon in a baking dish.Rub the butter into the flour and caster sugar, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough.Drop spoonfuls over the peaches and bake at 190°C until golden and bubbling.Serve warm with the cream.Fourth CourseFrankly-my-dear mint julepRhett walks away into the morning fog. Bourbon over crushed ice with fresh mint.How to make it240ml Kentucky bourbon1 cup mint leaves80g caster sugar80ml water4 cups crushed iceHeat the sugar and water until dissolved, add half the mint and cool.Pack 4 cups with crushed ice, add 60ml bourbon and a splash of strained syrup to each.Stir until frosted and crown with mint.Iced tea with peach and mintFor a long afternoon on the Twelve Oaks lawn.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
